overview: This bill requires the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to provide telehealth care and mail-order prescriptions, within one year, to veterans living in the Freely Associated States, the Pacific island nations of Micronesia, the Marshall Islands and Palau, which have special agreements with the United States. It also changes the VA's authority to pay travel costs for these veterans' care from optional to required within one year. The VA would have to report to Congress every three months on progress and costs. Separately, it extends by two months, to March 31, 2033, an existing limit on VA pension payments to certain veterans receiving Medicaid-covered nursing home care. The Senate passed it, and as of December 18, 2025, it was being held at the desk in the House.
for: Supporters say veterans in these Pacific nations, many of whom served in the U.S. military, currently have limited access to VA care, and telehealth, mail-order drugs and travel help would close that gap.
against: Critics say turning optional services into firm requirements adds new costs in remote locations where delivery may be difficult, and the bill does not set aside new money to pay for them.
